goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — An unavailable or malformed feed aborts retrieval before HTTP fallback, leaving otherwise reachable articles stuck on the loading screen.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 35-45, the perform_retrieve method first checks if feed_polling_enabled? and calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}). In lib/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the poll_feed method uses SimpleRSS.parse with open() which can raise exceptions if the feed URL is unavailable or malformed. If this raises an exception, the code never reaches the fetch_http call on line 50 of topic_retriever.rb. This means if RSS polling is enabled but the feed is broken/unavailable, the HTTP fallback (which could successfully retrieve the article directly) is never attempted, leaving users stuck on the loading screen. This is a real bug in the error handling flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — A worker interruption between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a permanent throttle key that prevents all subsequent nonstaff imports of that URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 24-30 that the code uses SETNX followed by EXPIRE as separate operations. If the process crashes or is interrupted between these two Redis commands, the key will be set but never expire, creating a permanent throttle that blocks all future non-staff imports of that specific URL. This is a real race condition bug - the atomic SETEX or SET with EX option should be used instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — Concurrent imports can interleave post and checksum writes, leaving mismatched content that later polls skip because its checksum already matches.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the import method in topic_embed.rb, the update path (lines 30-36) performs two separate operations: 1) revisor.revise! to update the post content, and 2) embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) to update the checksum. These are not wrapped in a transaction together. If two concurrent imports for the same URL occur, one could update the post content while another updates the checksum, leaving them mismatched. The creation path uses Topic.transaction but the update path does not have similar protection. This is a real race condition that could cause content/checksum mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65 — URL rewriting turns protocol-relative references such as `//cdn.example/image.png` into paths on the article host and leaves document-relative references unresolved, breaking imported links and images.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 53-72, the code only handles URLs that start_with?('/') for both href and src attributes. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example/image.png' don't start with a single '/', they start with '//', so they won't be matched by start_with?('/'). Wait, actually '//cdn.example' does start with '/' since start_with?('/') checks if the string begins with that character. However, the code then does: a['href'] = "#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}" which strips leading slashes and prepends the article host prefix. So '//cdn.example/image.png' would become 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example/image.png' which is incorrect - it should remain as '//cdn.example/image.png' or be converted to 'https://cdn.example/image.png'. This is a real bug where protocol-relative URLs are incorrectly rewritten.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — Existing installations have this zero-byte migration already recorded, so the new topic_embeds table is never created and embed lookups/imports fail.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that existing installations have a 'zero-byte migration already recorded' but the diff shows this is a NEW migration file being created (20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb). The migration file contains proper content with create_table and add_index statements. There's no evidence in the diff of any 'zero-byte' issue or that this migration was previously recorded. The migration appears to be a standard new migration that will run normally on existing installations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Existing installations have this zero-byte migration already recorded, so cook_method is never added and imported-post creation fails.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that existing installations have a 'zero-byte migration already recorded' but there's no evidence in the diff to support this. The migration file db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb is shown as a new file being added (indicated by 'new file mode' in the diff), and it contains valid migration code that adds the cook_method column. The finding appears to be speculating about deployment scenarios not evidenced in the diff itself. The migration is properly structured and would work correctly for new installations. Any issues with existing installations having recorded migrations would be an operational/deployment concern, not a code defect visible in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — TopicEmbed.import's regex accepts `http://` while TopicRetriever rejects it via URI.host, so direct feed and Disqus callers can persist embeds under a different URL contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a URL contract mismatch between TopicEmbed.import's regex and TopicRetriever's URI.host check. Looking at the diff: TopicEmbed.import (line 11) uses `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` which accepts both http:// and https:// URLs. TopicRetriever.invalid_host? compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` - this extracts the host from the URL, not rejecting http://. Both methods work with full URLs containing http:// or https://. The finding misreads the code - there's no contract mismatch where one accepts and one rejects http:// URLs. URI(@embed_url).host simply extracts the hostname portion, it doesn't reject URLs based on scheme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Reusing the scheduled PollFeed job as a synchronous retriever couples cache-miss handling to job lifecycle, so later scheduling changes can silently change request-time importing.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a design concern in lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 where `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` is called synchronously within `perform_retrieve`. This creates coupling between the request-time topic retrieval and the scheduled job's implementation. Looking at the diff, the PollFeed job (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) is designed as a scheduled job with `recurrence { hourly }`, but TopicRetriever reuses it synchronously. This is a legitimate architectural concern - if PollFeed's behavior changes (e.g., adding rate limiting, changing how it processes feeds), it could affect the synchronous retrieval path unexpectedly. This is a valid scope/architecture concern grounded in the actual code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key is never called, so its cache-like name and Digest dependency imply a freshness guard that polling does not actually have.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `feed_key` method is defined on lines 20-22 but never called anywhere in the diff. The method generates a cache key using Digest::SHA1, suggesting it was intended for some kind of freshness/deduplication check during polling, but the `poll_feed` method doesn't use it. This is dead code that suggests incomplete implementation - either the freshness guard was intended but not implemented, or this is leftover code. This is a legitimate code review concern about unused code and potentially missing functionality, but not a bug since the polling still works, just without the implied caching mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Every first-time embed URL executes the full RSS import; the per-URL throttle does not share a feed-level cache, so traffic across distinct pages multiplies all-item database work and can saturate workers.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real architectural concern in the diff. Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb:41, the perform_retrieve method calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) which processes ALL RSS items (as seen in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb lines 27-35 where it iterates through rss.items.each). The throttle in retrieved_recently? (lines 24-32) is per-URL based on 'retrieved:#{@embed_url}', so each unique embed URL that triggers retrieval will execute the full RSS import. This is a legitimate scalability/architecture concern - multiple distinct page embeds could cause redundant full feed processing. However, this is not strictly a bug since the system will still function correctly, just inefficiently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — Disabling Sidekiq retries drops a transient feed fetch or parse failure, leaving imports stale until the next hourly run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `sidekiq_options retry: false` on line 12 of poll_feed.rb. This is a deliberate design choice that disables automatic retries for the scheduled job. The finding correctly identifies that transient failures (network issues, temporary feed unavailability) won't be retried until the next hourly run. This is a valid architectural concern about the new feed polling feature - it's not a bug per se since the code works as written, but it's a legitimate review point about resilience of the new embedding/feed import functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — The feed HTTP fetch has no explicit timeout, so a stalled feed can tie up worker capacity and stop imports.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29, the code uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` from the 'open-uri' library (required at line 7) without specifying any timeout options. The open-uri library's `open` method can indeed hang indefinitely on a stalled connection if no timeout is specified. This is a real defect - a scheduled job that hangs can tie up Sidekiq worker capacity. The finding correctly identifies the specific line and the actual problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The remote page fetch has no explicit timeout, so an unresponsive embed source can exhaust retrieval workers and leave embeds loading.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the code uses `open(url).read` from the 'open-uri' library without specifying any timeout options. This is a real defect - if the remote server is slow or unresponsive, the worker thread will block indefinitely. The same pattern appears in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27 with `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. This can exhaust worker threads and cause the embed retrieval system to hang. This is a verifiable bug in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — RSS content is stored as unsanitized raw HTML, allowing feed-supplied scripts or event handlers to execute in the forum origin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and in post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method simply returns `raw` without any sanitization. The RSS content from poll_feed.rb (line 33: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) is passed through TopicEmbed.import and stored as raw HTML. While CGI.unescapeHTML decodes HTML entities, it does not sanitize malicious content. This allows feed-supplied scripts or event handlers to execute in the forum's origin context, which is a real XSS security vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The no-embed test expects TopicRetriever directly although best enqueues :retrieve_topic, so it fails and does not verify the loading path.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in embed_controller.rb line 14-15, when topic_id is nil, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` to enqueue a background job, then renders 'loading'. However, the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43-47 sets up expectations directly on TopicRetriever (`TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`), but the controller doesn't call TopicRetriever directly - it enqueues a job. The job (in app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) is what calls TopicRetriever. So the test's expectations on TopicRetriever will never be satisfied by the controller action, making this a real test bug where the test doesn't properly verify the loading path behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — No spec exercises this job, so missing embed_url rejection and staff throttle propagation can regress without detection.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new job class `RetrieveTopic` in `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` lacks dedicated test coverage. Looking at the diff, there's no spec file for this job (no `spec/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic_spec.rb`). The job contains logic for parameter validation (`raise Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:embed_url) unless args[:embed_url].present?`) and staff throttle propagation (`no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`). While `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` tests the `TopicRetriever` class, it doesn't exercise the job wrapper that calls it. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for new nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24 — The poll-feed specs mock poll_feed and never parse an item or call TopicEmbed.import, leaving the link/id fallback and imported content behavior unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the poll_feed_spec.rb tests only verify that poll_feed is called under certain conditions by mocking it (poller.expects(:poll_feed)), but never actually tests the implementation of poll_feed itself. Looking at the diff, poll_feed in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb contains non-trivial logic including RSS parsing, URL extraction with fallback (url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//), and content processing. The spec file shows all tests use 'poller.expects(:poll_feed).never' or 'poller.expects(:poll_feed).once' without ever testing the actual parsing behavior. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:20 — The retriever specs stub retrieved_recently? and perform_retrieve, leaving Redis throttling, existing-topic short circuit, feed fallback, and remote import without behavioral coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the TopicRetriever specs (spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb) stub out `retrieved_recently?` and `perform_retrieve` methods, which means the actual implementation of Redis throttling (lines 24-32 in lib/topic_retriever.rb), the existing-topic short circuit (line 37), feed fallback (lines 40-43), and remote import (fetch_http method) are not tested with real behavioral coverage. The specs only verify that perform_retrieve is called/not called based on host validation and throttle checks, but don't test the actual behavior of these methods. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.
